speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dysuria. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID).

The clinical picture of severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dysuria, and post-coital pain in a sexually active 17-year-old is highly suggestive of an ascending infection. Given the severity of the symptoms (vomiting and severe pain), I need to confirm the diagnosis immediately.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic Ultrasound
REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Pregnancy Test, CBC, and Cervical Swab for GC/Chlamydia
